description: Retrieval evaluation set for the C Structured Programming assistant. Each query has exactly one gold chunk id. Corpus mimics lecture/lab PDF chunks (mostly English, as course slides usually are, plus a few Arabic notes).

corpus.text: Lecture 1: Variables and Data Types. A variable is a named memory location. In C every variable must be declared before use: int age = 20; float price = 9.5; char grade = 'A'; double pi = 3.14159; The int type stores whole numbers (usually 4 bytes), float stores single-precision real numbers (4 bytes), double stores double-precision real numbers (8 bytes) and char stores a single character (1 byte). Use sizeof(int) to print the size of a type on your machine.

Constants in C. A constant is a value that cannot change during program execution. You can define a constant with the preprocessor: #define PI 3.14 or with the const keyword: const int MAX = 100; Trying to assign a new value to a const variable causes a compilation error. By convention constant names are written in UPPERCASE.

Lecture 2: Operators and Expressions. Arithmetic operators: + - * / %. The modulus operator % gives the remainder of integer division, for example 7 % 3 equals 1. When both operands are integers, / performs integer division: 7 / 2 equals 3, not 3.5. Increment and decrement: x++ uses the value then increases it, ++x increases first then uses it.

Type casting. To force a conversion from one type to another write the target type in parentheses: float avg = (float) sum / count; Without the cast, sum / count is computed as integer division and the fractional part is lost. Implicit conversion also happens when mixing int and double in one expression: the int is promoted to double.

Lecture 3: Input and Output. printf prints formatted output to the screen and scanf reads input from the keyboard. Format specifiers: %d for int, %f for float, %lf for double with scanf, %c for char, %s for strings. In scanf you must pass the address of the variable using the & operator: scanf("%d", &x); Forgetting & is a very common mistake that crashes the program. Use \n to print a new line.

Lecture 4: Decision Making with if. The if statement executes a block only when its condition is true (non-zero). if (marks >= 50) { printf("Pass"); } else { printf("Fail"); } You can chain conditions with else if. Relational operators: == != > < >= <=. Logical operators: && (and), || (or), ! (not).

The switch statement selects one of many cases based on the value of an integer or char expression. switch (choice) { case 1: printf("Add"); break; case 2: printf("Subtract"); break; default: printf("Invalid"); } If you forget break, execution falls through to the next case. The default case runs when no case matches. switch cannot be used with float values or ranges.

Lecture 5: Loops - the for loop. A for loop has three parts: initialization; condition; update. for (int i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { printf("%d ", i); } prints the numbers from 1 to 10. Use a for loop when the number of iterations is known in advance. The loop variable can also count down: for (i = 10; i > 0; i--).

The while loop checks its condition before each iteration and repeats as long as the condition is true. int n = 5; while (n > 0) { printf("%d\n", n); n--; } If the condition is false at the start, the body never executes. Make sure something inside the loop changes the condition, otherwise you get an infinite loop.

The do-while loop checks its condition after the body, so the body always executes at least once. do { printf("Enter a positive number: "); scanf("%d", &num); } while (num <= 0); This makes do-while ideal for input validation and menus. Note the semicolon after while (condition);

Nested loops. A loop inside another loop. The inner loop completes all its iterations for every single iteration of the outer loop. Example printing a right triangle of stars: for (i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { for (j = 1; j <= i; j++) printf("*"); printf("\n"); } Nested loops are used for patterns, multiplication tables and 2D arrays.

break and continue inside loops. break exits the loop immediately. continue skips the rest of the current iteration and jumps to the next one. for (i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { if (i % 2 == 0) continue; printf("%d ", i); } prints only the odd numbers 1 3 5 7 9.

Lecture 6: Arrays. An array stores a fixed number of elements of the same type in contiguous memory. int marks[5] = {90, 80, 70, 60, 50}; Indexes start at 0, so the first element is marks[0] and the last is marks[4]. Accessing marks[5] is out of bounds: C does not check this and the behavior is undefined. Use a for loop to traverse an array.

Two-dimensional arrays represent tables or matrices. int m[3][4]; has 3 rows and 4 columns. Access an element with m[row][col]. Traverse with nested loops: for (i = 0; i < 3; i++) for (j = 0; j < 4; j++) sum += m[i][j];

Lecture 7: Strings. In C a string is an array of char terminated by the null character '\0'. char name[20] = "Ali"; The array must have room for the terminating '\0'. Useful functions from <string.h>: strlen returns the length without '\0', strcpy copies, strcmp compares, strcat concatenates. Read a full line with fgets(name, 20, stdin); scanf("%s") stops at the first space.

Lecture 8: Functions. A function is a named block of code that performs a task. It has a return type, a name and parameters: int add(int a, int b) { return a + b; } Declare a function prototype before main: int add(int a, int b); A void function returns no value. Functions make programs modular and avoid repeating code.

Variable scope. Local variables are declared inside a function and exist only while the function runs. Global variables are declared outside all functions and are visible everywhere. Parameters are local copies: C passes arguments by value, so changing a parameter inside a function does not change the caller's variable.

Lecture 9: Pointers. A pointer is a variable that stores the memory address of another variable. int x = 10; int *p = &x; The & operator gives the address and the * operator dereferences the pointer: *p = 20; changes x to 20. To let a function modify the caller's variables pass their addresses: void swap(int *a, int *b) { int t = *a; *a = *b; *b = t; }

Recursion. A recursive function calls itself. Every recursive function needs a base case that stops the recursion. int fact(int n) { if (n <= 1) return 1; return n * fact(n - 1); } Without a base case the program keeps calling itself until a stack overflow occurs.

Algorithms: Linear search. To find a key in an unsorted array, compare it with each element from the first to the last. int search(int a[], int n, int key) { for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) if (a[i] == key) return i; return -1; } It returns the index of the key or -1 if not found. In the worst case it checks all n elements.

Algorithms: Bubble sort. Repeatedly compare adjacent elements and swap them if they are in the wrong order. After each pass the largest remaining element moves to the end. for (i = 0; i < n - 1; i++) for (j = 0; j < n - 1 - i; j++) if (a[j] > a[j + 1]) { t = a[j]; a[j] = a[j + 1]; a[j + 1] = t; }

Common mistakes in C. Using = (assignment) instead of == (comparison) inside if: if (x = 5) is always true. Putting a semicolon right after if (...); or for (...); makes the body empty. Forgetting to initialize a sum variable to 0. Missing break in switch. Using an uninitialized variable gives garbage values.

Lab 1 - Exercise 3: Write a program that reads a positive integer N and prints the sum of all even numbers from 1 to N. Hint: use a for loop and the % operator to test if a number is even. Sample input: 10 Sample output: Sum = 30

Lab 2 - Exercise 1: Read 10 integers into an array and find the largest element and its position. Start by assuming the first element is the maximum, then compare it with the remaining elements inside a loop. Print: Max = ... at index ...

Lab 3 - Exercise 2: Write a function long factorial(int n) that returns n! using a loop, and call it from main for a number entered by the user. Then write a second version using recursion and compare the two.

Lab 4 - Exercise 1: Grade calculator. Read a student's mark (0-100) and print the letter grade: A for 90 and above, B for 80-89, C for 70-79, D for 60-69, F below 60. Solve it once with if-else if and once with switch using mark / 10 as the switch expression.

Lab 5 - Exercise 4: Read a word from the user and print it reversed without using library functions other than strlen. Example: input hello, output olleh. Hint: loop from the last index (length - 1) down to 0.

Lab 6 - Exercise 2: Temperature conversion table. Use a while loop to print Celsius values from 0 to 100 in steps of 10 together with their Fahrenheit equivalents using F = C * 9 / 5 + 32. Print the results formatted in two columns.

ملاحظات المعيد: الفرق بين حلقات التكرار. حلقة for نستخدمها عندما نعرف عدد مرات التكرار مسبقاً. حلقة while تفحص الشرط قبل التنفيذ لذلك قد لا تنفذ أبداً. حلقة do-while تنفذ جسم الحلقة مرة واحدة على الأقل لأن الشرط يفحص في النهاية.

ملاحظات المعيد: مراحل تشغيل برنامج C. أولاً نكتب الكود في ملف بامتداد .c ثم يقوم المترجم compiler بتحويله إلى ملف تنفيذي. أخطاء الترجمة compilation errors مثل نسيان الفاصلة المنقوطة تظهر قبل التشغيل، أما أخطاء التشغيل runtime errors فتظهر أثناء تنفيذ البرنامج.
